$comment: The two runs the current harness produced, as the landing page shows them. Hand-written rather than generated: these ran in a user's own Java project, which is where the harness is meant to work, so there is no artifact in this repository to derive them from. scripts/test/contracts.test.mjs asserts the figures here also appear in README.md, because two places holding the same numbers is how they drift.

flows.$comment: The recorded revision flows, as the landing page plays them. Each entry is one run replayed revision by revision: the left panel is the reference, the right is what the harness rendered, and the rail underneath is every revision it took. Nothing in either frame is regenerated imagery. Hand-written for the same reason as `runs` above — these ran in a user's own Java project, so there is no artifact in this repository to derive them from — and scripts/test/contracts.test.mjs asserts the revision counts here also appear in README.md.

items.title: Invoice
items.subtitle: flowing table, repeated header, page numbering
items.headline: 12 revisions, 113 minutes.
items.body: The first two did not compile, which is the point of recording them: revision-001 and revision-002 are FAILED and still on disk, with what broke and what was tried. The last two were plain sentences with no instructions attached.
items.quote: the dividers disappeared, for some reason

items.title: Professional sidebar CV
items.subtitle: photo, sidebar, timeline rail
items.headline: 10 revisions, 120 minutes.
items.body: From a screenshot and the sentence “Create this screenshot as a GraphCompose template.” The corrections in the second half are the ones worth reading: initials that must derive from the name rather than be hardcoded, a LinkedIn href that has to apply to the icon as well as the text, a timeline rail that should not run above its first marker.

items.title: Charcoal and gold CV
items.subtitle: dark sidebar, rated skill rows, timeline rail
items.headline: 9 revisions, and the ninth was one sentence.
items.body: The loop declared itself ready at revision-008, after seven passes that each named one thing and fixed it — calibrate the type scale, drop the main column’s uniform 9px offset, seat the skill bullets in their own column. Then one sentence closed it. No duration is quoted here: the session stayed open across a long gap, so the telemetry measures the window rather than the work.
items.quote: the timeline ring should close over the rail, not let it pass through

runs.title: Two-column CV
runs.subtitle: photo, navy sidebar, timeline rail
runs.correctionSummary: Both about the timeline: the rail overran its markers, and a job title drifted off centre.
runs.note: Twice the loop could not tell a layout fault from a painting fault, so it wrote a probe — a throwaway document that renders one arrangement and measures the pixels — and settled it. Both findings are recorded observations now, with probes that re-confirm them.

runs.title: Single-column CV
runs.subtitle: display serif, proportional skill bars, icon rows
runs.correctionSummary: Three plain sentences about what looked wrong, none explaining how to fix it.
runs.quote: just the certification and achievement divider — vertical

caveat: Neither run was pixel-perfect from one request, and the pixel-similarity figure stayed unimpressive in both: the references are rasterised in typefaces no bundled family reproduces, so glyph edges dominate the comparison. The images are the evidence; the score is not.
